open_obligations: Note the unequal number of turns between debate (3) and market-making (1).
Note that the supervisor is a model, not a non-expert human as in sandwiching.
Check that the four tasks have a strong-weak gap large enough for a sandwiching analogy.
out.other_title: Do debate, market-making and recursive reward modeling work in sandwiching trials?
out.rationale: Bowman et al. ask for empirical trials of debate and market-making. Lang, Huang and Li report that replacing debate with market-making or consultancy as context for training the weak model gives lower test accuracy and PGR on all four tasks; the 'weak supervisor' is a 7B model trained on transcripts, not a human, and market-making and consultancy run for one turn while debate runs for three.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether debate and market-making differ as sources of information for a weak supervisor, for Qwen-14B agents and Qwen-7B weak models on NLP classification

text: The paper reports that replacing debate with consultancy (one consultant assigned a random answer) or market-making (one debater arguing for the answer the weak supervisor did not select) gives lower test accuracy and PGR on all four tasks, and the authors note that consultancy is a relatively weak baseline because the consultant argues for the incorrect answer half the time.
title: Debate beats consultancy and market-making as the source of weak-model context
